original.text: avyaktanāmnī parameśaśaktir anādyavidyā triguṇātmikā parā / kāryānumeyā sudhiyaiva māyā yayā jagat sarvam idaṃ prasūyate
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Māyā, called the unmanifest, is the power of the supreme Lord, beginningless ignorance consisting of the three guṇas, superior (to its effects), to be inferred by the wise from its effects; by it this whole world is produced.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: sannāpy asannāpy ubhayātmikā no bhinnāpy abhinnāpy ubhayātmikā no / sāṅgāpy anaṅgā hy ubhayātmikā no mahādbhutānirvacanīyarūpā
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: It is neither existent nor non-existent nor both; neither different nor non-different nor both; neither with parts nor partless nor both; it is most wonderful and of indescribable nature.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: cittasya śuddhaye karma na tu vastūpalabdhaye / vastusiddhir vicāreṇa na kiṃcit karmakoṭibhiḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Action is for the purification of the mind, not for attaining the Reality; the Reality is attained through inquiry, not by millions of acts.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: Ignorance has two powers: the veiling power (āvaraṇa) of tamas, which hides the self, and the projecting power (vikṣepa) of rajas, which projects the world and the ego's activity.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: brahma satyaṃ jagan mithyety evaṃrūpo viniścayaḥ / so 'yaṃ nityānityavastuvivekaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: The firm conviction 'Brahman is real, the world is false' is called discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: The six virtues defined: calm (śama) is resting the mind on its goal after detaching it from objects; self-control (dama) is turning the organs back to their sources; withdrawal (uparati) is the mind's not depending on external things; forbearance (titikṣā) is enduring all afflictions without seeking redress and without anxiety; faith (śraddhā) is firm trust in the words of scripture and teacher; concentration (samādhāna) is fixing the intellect steadily on Brahman; longing for liberation (mumukṣutva) is the desire to be freed from bondage by knowing one's true nature.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: Through the tendency toward the world, the tendency toward (pedantic) learning and the tendency toward the body, right knowledge does not arise; these three tendencies are iron fetters.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: durlabhaṃ trayam evaitad devānugrahahetukam / manuṣyatvaṃ mumukṣutvaṃ mahāpuruṣasaṃśrayaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: These three are rare and come only by divine grace: human birth, the longing for liberation, and the refuge of a great soul.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: mokṣakāraṇasāmagryāṃ bhaktir eva garīyasī / svasvarūpānusandhānaṃ bhaktir ity abhidhīyate
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Among the means to liberation devotion (bhakti) is supreme; devotion is said to be the constant searching into (dwelling on) one's own true nature.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

original.text: śāntā mahānto nivasanti santo vasantaval lokahitaṃ carantaḥ / tīrṇāḥ svayaṃ bhīmabhavārṇavaṃ janān ahetunānyān api tārayantaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: There are peaceful, great-souled good people who, having crossed the terrible ocean of becoming, live like the spring season doing good to the world and help others across without any motive.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: Prajñā (steady wisdom) is the mental mode, free of conceptual distinctions and of the nature of pure consciousness, that apprehends the identity of Brahman and the self when both have been purified (of adjuncts).
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: Prārabdha is strong even for the knower and is exhausted only by experience: an arrow shot at an object taken for a tiger does not stop when one sees it is a cow; knowledge burns the accumulated and future karma but not the karma that has already begun.
notes: The discussion of prārabdha spans c. vv. 451–464; the arrow image is recalled with moderate confidence and its numbers with low. Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.

paraphrase: Faith, devotion and the yoga of meditation are declared by scripture as the direct causes of liberation for the seeker; one who abides in them is freed from the bondage of the body imagined by ignorance.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution disputed). Verse numbers follow the common (Mādhavānanda) numbering; other editions differ by one or two.
